title: Controlling blood glucose
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest card, sci-blood-glucose-diabetes, teaches only insulin and diabetes and never covers glucagon, while the other two cards cover both hormones at Biology depth beyond Years 9 and 10, so none fits the brief as it is or with small changes.

draft.title: Controlling blood glucose
card: Cells use glucose from the blood for energy. The body keeps the level of blood glucose within a narrow range.
released by the pancreas when blood glucose rises, such as after a meal. It lowers blood glucose.
released by the pancreas when blood glucose falls, such as between meals. It raises blood glucose.
Each hormone is released in response to the change it corrects, so the level returns towards its normal range.
draft.remember: Glucose up: insulin brings it down. Glucose down: glucagon brings it up.

a.q: Which pair correctly matches the hormone with its effect on blood glucose?
opts: Insulin lowers it and glucagon raises it
Insulin raises it and glucagon lowers it
Both insulin and glucagon lower it
Both insulin and glucagon raise it
a.why: Insulin lowers blood glucose and glucagon raises it, so together they keep it steady. Swapping them is a common mistake, but insulin is the one released when glucose is high.
a.clue: Insulin is released after a meal.

b.q: Tom skips lunch and does not eat for six hours at his school in Ballarat. What would his pancreas do as his blood glucose falls?
opts: Release glucagon, which raises blood glucose
Release insulin, which raises blood glucose
Release glucagon, which lowers blood glucose
Release insulin, which lowers blood glucose
b.why: Falling blood glucose triggers the pancreas to release glucagon, which raises it. Insulin is tempting because it is the better known hormone, but it lowers blood glucose and is released when the level rises.
b.clue: The pancreas responds to the change in the level.

a.best: Insulin lowers it and glucagon raises it

b.best: Release glucagon, which raises blood glucose
